strategy.title: No plan: no price trucking fleet managers are shown to pay for the maintenance workbook
strategy.why: The opening's only price evidence is Software Advice's figure that HVAC field-service management software costs $1,200 a year per technician seat - a different buyer population (HVAC contractors), a different product (recurring SaaS seat) and a different billing basis. It does not show what regional trucking fleet managers pay for a one-off preventive-maintenance scheduling workbook. Every other link (reach, dated demand, measured 6% paid pre-order conversion, Brain-produced spreadsheet at $10 cost, 7-day settlement, 600 fleets) is evidenced.

alternatives.title: Sell the workbook at $1,200 to 5 fleets
alternatives.why: Rejected: $1,200 is an HVAC software seat price from another population, not a price fleet managers pay for this workbook; the target would rest on it entirely.

steps.label: Research what regional trucking fleets are published as paying for preventive-maintenance scheduling tools or workbooks, with source and date
With an evidenced fleet price, re-run the plan: deals = ceil($5,000 / price) from 600 fleets

noPlan.decisiveGap: OFFER_AND_PRICE: no price regional trucking fleet managers are shown to pay for the workbook; the only figure is an annual per-seat price for HVAC field-service software, a different population and product.
noPlan.resolution: Brain researches the parked revenueRange question for trucking fleets specifically (published prices for preventive-maintenance scheduling tools or templates, with source and date) and re-runs the plan with that price; if none is found, a zero-capital priced pre-order test to fleet managers measures it.

excluded.why: Price evidence is from HVAC contractors' software seats, not trucking fleets buying this workbook

review.reasons: NO_PLAN is right. The only price evidence is Software Advice's $1,200/year per-technician-seat figure for HVAC field-service software: another population (HVAC contractors), another product (recurring SaaS seat) and another billing basis, so it is not a price regional trucking fleet managers pay for a one-off maintenance workbook. All other links (600 fleets, dated demand, 6% measured paid pre-order conversion on the offer's own page, $10 Brain-produced spreadsheet, 7-day settlement) are evidenced. Decisive gap OFFER_AND_PRICE is named correctly; resolution is research then a zero-capital priced pre-order test.
